entries.name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
entries.reason: Own drawn frames: the elbow fixed at (51.55, 16.8) - the raised upper arm holds 12.5 exactly - while the forearm folds from a 50-degree stretch (the hands behind the head, on the back of the head so the face stays clear) to 173 degrees at the extension. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a cable rope overhead triceps extension.

frames.caption: Hold the rope overhead with the elbows aiming through one steady line.
Let the hands travel behind the head under control.
Feel the stretch at the bottom of the range.
Extend through the forearms only.
Finish with the arms long and the elbows quiet.

entries.name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing showed an overhead extension with the upper arms beside the head, which is a different movement. Source-bound side-view draft: standing facing a high pulley with one handle in the near hand; the upper arm stays locked against the side while the forearm straightens from an elbow bent tighter than a right angle to straight down beside the body, a one-second squeeze, and a slower return. The free arm hangs. The cable only lengthens as the arm straightens. One arm is shown; the last caption carries the change of arms. Not drawn: the underhand grip.
entries.summary: Facing a high pulley with one handle in an underhand grip and the upper arm pinned to your side, straighten the arm down beside you, squeeze for a second, return slowly, then change arms.

frames.caption: Stand facing a high pulley and take a single handle in one hand with an underhand grip, palm facing up, then pull it down until the upper arm is locked against your side with the elbow bent tighter than a right angle.
Keeping the upper arm still, straighten the arm down beside you.
Squeeze the triceps for a second.
Return slowly to the start.
Complete the repetitions, then change arms.

entries.name: Dumbbell Tricep Extension -Pronated Grip
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing showed a standing overhead extension, which is a different movement. Source-bound side-view draft: lying on a flat bench with the feet on the floor, a dumbbell in each hand straight above the shoulders; the upper arms stay upright while the elbows bend to lower the dumbbells slowly beside the ears, and straighten again. The palms face the feet, shown by the dumbbells reading end-on.
entries.summary: Lying on a flat bench with the dumbbells above the shoulders and the palms toward your feet, bend only the elbows to lower them slowly beside your ears, then straighten the arms.

frames.caption: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells directly above the shoulders with the arms straight, palms facing toward your feet and the elbows tucked in close.
Keeping the upper arms still and the grip unchanged, bend the elbows to lower the dumbbells slowly until they are beside your ears.
Elbows tucked in, upper arms vertical.
Straighten the arms to return to the start.
Lower slowly to the ears.

entries.name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
entries.reason: Own drawn frames: the same overhead chain with the dumbbell drawn across at the hands (the bell lies along the forearm), which is the visual difference from the end-on pronated version beside it. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a standing dumbbell overhead triceps extension.

frames.caption: Hold the dumbbell overhead with the elbows tucked.
Lower into the stretch under control.
Pause where the triceps lengthens.
Press the bell back overhead through the forearms.
Finish tall with the bell steady overhead.

entries.name: Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension
entries.reason: Own drawn frames: the same overhead chain with the barbell drawn END-ON at the hands (Entry 0181 - the plate pairs ride the wrists), the family tell against the dumbbell versions. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a standing overhead barbell triceps extension.

frames.caption: Hold the barbell overhead with the elbows narrow.
Lower the bar behind the head slowly.
Keep the bar path the same every rep.
Extend through the forearms without moving the elbows.
Finish with the bar locked over the shoulders.
